judgements.justification: A's AC said after discussion all agreed presentation and positioning were the main weak point, which nsKx confirmed; it ignored the accept-side scores but misstated no reviewer's position, and B's overstatement ran toward the higher tier.
No committee called the paper of narrow interest; B's 'too large for a conference' remark came from the spotlight committee and did not cap its tier.
B's misreading detractor r4iB was corrected and raised its score, and B's AC gave a spotlight; no chair argued only for acceptance against a misreading score.
The authors posted no new experiments or analyses on either forum; both committees received only promises of restructuring and tightness experiments.
A's reviewers all rated at confidence 3, and B's most confident reviewer, r4iB (confidence 4), gave B's lowest score, so no high-confidence expert was outvoted toward a lower tier.
No reviewer added a new objection after the response period; jeQC's 2021-08-24 comment kept its score and the authors answered it on 2021-08-25.

The rating gap follows the rebuttal: B's reviewers stated that the promised changes or corrections addressed their concerns, while A's detractors said theirs were not answered, so the verbal assessments differ too.
A objected to unclear positioning and a weaker rate than Arora et al., not to an overstated headline or title, and no reviewer asked to narrow the 'first' claim.
B's unsure reviewers (hENG, DACB) gave 7s inside a spotlight decision, and A's reviewers all rated at confidence 3; no flat marginal-accept scores held a committee to a poster.
